# GT13b scanner reuse differential review

Baseline: `7eafe27`; reviewed the worker worktree's four modified files and new `scanner_reuse_test.go`. Fathom `review_diff` timed out after five seconds against an index lacking worker edits; all findings below come from the actual diff. Read-only source review, no builds/native trial performed.

## Blockers

**F1 -- Complete CUE receipts can omit coverage (`schema.cue:52-64,83,102`).** The new equation is conditional on optional `reuse`. A purported complete receipt with `expectedFiles=2`, `completedFiles=1`, no `reuse`, and otherwise valid fields satisfies the displayed constraints, although one logical scanner input has no witness. This affects ordinary/compact file and Git variants. The negative tests only change `reuse.files`; none removes `reuse`. Require exactly one complete shape: absent reuse implies `completedFiles == expectedFiles`; present reuse implies `completedFiles + reuse.files == expectedFiles`. Retain partial inequality on blocked/incomplete receipts. This is a schema/receipt integrity gap, not evidence that the production Go scanner produces that forged receipt.

**F2 -- Full-corpus mutation witness amplifies work (`scanner.go:330-340,352,359,388,430`).** `unchanged()` rehashes *all* selected bytes multiple times per input, even with `reuseEqualInputs=false`. A valid 32-file/64-MiB request can hash roughly 6 GiB with reuse disabled and roughly 8 GiB enabled; a 32-row Git diff may contain up to 129 scanner units and amplify further. This consumes the same 30-second scanner deadline and can turn formerly complete inputs into deadline holds. It also threatens OR-A10's unique-input overhead bar. Check each current input before/after its call plus all inputs once before success/disclosure, or another linear-cost witness that still catches persistent mutation of prior/future slices. Measure worst bounded corpus as well as the five paired trials. This is a concrete cost regression; a specific timeout was not measured here.

## Coverage and limits

Start-witness repair checks both version and input `started`; a nonstarted clean fake cannot increment completion. Cache uses private `bytes.Clone` values, SHA indexing plus byte equality, <=256 entries/8 MiB retained content, ordinary scan on cap exhaustion, and actual-versus-reused counters. Deadline checks bracket hits; cleanup failure overrides success. Git's representation is appended as a scanner input. Its current maximum is below the CUE 256-unit bound (32 diff rows x at most four units plus representation = 129), so no off-by-one finding. Enabled file/Git late-finding tests withhold rows/selector fields. Disabled mode omits `reuse` on the wire, but now pays the mutation hashing cost. Worker focused race/CUE results are reported in its receipt; I did not rerun them. Native deterministic agreement, full gate and publication remain root-owned.
